drafts.question: What red flags turned up in the bank accounts of persons of interest connected to a Philippine offshore gaming operator that was actually running scam operations?
drafts.summary: The relevant case is the APG Yearly Typologies Report 2025 case study on \"POGO X\" (Philippines), a licensed-looking offshore gaming operator that was in fact running crypto investment and romance (\"pig butchering\") scams with trafficked workers. AMLC's financial analysis of the persons of interest found accounts holding amounts reaching billions of pesos, and flagged two specific patterns: (1) a significant jump in both transaction volume and amounts in a POI's accounts coinciding with the inception of the POGOs, and (2) a substantial number of foreign exchange transactions funded by cash or cheque deposits made on or near the date of the exchange. Note that the passage in the corpus is truncated mid-list, so any further bullets are not retrievable. Related findings include that two POIs had recently been convicted in another jurisdiction's largest money laundering case, and that one POI and relatives left the country despite an Immigration Lookout Bulletin Order, prompting Egmont Secure Web requests to foreign FIUs.

claims.text: The case appears in the APG Yearly Typologies Report 2025 (Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering) as a Philippines-sourced case study concerning "POGO X", which operated under the guise of a legitimate offshore gaming corporation while actually running cryptocurrency investment scams and romance scams ("pig butchering") using trafficked workers who posed as attractive males or females on social media.

The raid was instigated by the Philippine FIU, the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), through intelligence gathering and financial analysis directed at the POGO and its persons of interest (POIs), alongside Philippine Senate public hearings.
AMLC's financial analysis found that the amounts involved in the accounts of the various persons of interest reached billions of pesos.
Red flag 1: there was a significant increase in both the transaction volume and the amounts involved in a POI's accounts coinciding with the inception of the POGOs.
Red flag 2: a substantial number of foreign exchange transactions were funded by cash or cheque deposits made on or near the date of the exchange.
The list of initial findings in the retrieved passage is cut off after the second bullet, so any further red flags in the original report are not available in the corpus.

Related adverse-information findings in the same case: two of the POIs had recently been convicted in the biggest money laundering case in another jurisdiction (Jurisdiction B), and AMLC sought information on their possible links to foreign fugitives involved in that case via the Egmont Secure Web.

One of the POIs, together with cohorts and siblings, reportedly left the Philippines despite being subject to an Immigration Lookout Bulletin Order and travelled to three Asian jurisdictions, prompting AMLC to request foreign FIU assistance on their financial transactions, travel records and properties.
AMLC also profiled the POIs' businesses, affiliations, assets and derogatory records as part of the investigation.
